title: Fibre dimension bounds descend to a finite stage
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $(X_i\to S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of finite-type morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] such that for $i\le j$ the canonical map $X_j\to X_i\times_{S_i}S_j$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $X\to S$ be its limit. Fix an integer $d\ge0$. If every fibre of $X\to S$ has topological dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then for some $i$ every fibre of $X_i\to S_i$ has dimension at most $d$.

mathlib_searches.query: For an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions and closed immersion transition maps, if the limit morphism has fibres of dimension at most d then some finite stage has fibres of dimension at most d
mathlib_searches.results: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.compactSpace_of_isLimit; Scheme.exists_isAffine_of_isLimit; no theorem asserting fibre-dimension descent

mathlib_searches.query: dimension of fibres descends to a finite stage in an inverse limit of schemes with affine transitions
mathlib_searches.results: AffineTransitionLimit limit and morphism approximation lemmas; no fibre-dimension theorem
